seoTitle: How to Enter Medical Expenses in TurboTax
metaDescription: Find the medical expenses section in TurboTax, see what the IRS actually lets you deduct, and understand why the 7.5% AGI threshold means a modest total often changes nothing.
intro:
TurboTax will happily take every medical receipt you hand it, but that doesn't mean any of it lowers your bill. The IRS only lets you deduct the amount above 7.5% of your adjusted gross income, and only if you itemize instead of taking the standard deduction. A lot of people enter a few hundred dollars, see no change in their refund, and assume the software is broken.

This guide covers where the section actually lives, what counts as a qualifying expense under IRS rules, and why that threshold matters more than the entry screen itself.
prerequisites: A running total of what you paid this year for medical care, dental care, prescriptions, and medical travel, since TurboTax asks for a total per category rather than individual receipts
Records of any amount already reimbursed by insurance or an HSA, so you don't enter money you didn't actually pay out of pocket

steps.heading: Start from Tax Home
steps.body: Tax Home is the screen TurboTax opens to when you log back into a return in progress. It shows an "Up next" card for wherever you left off, plus a checklist down the left side: My Info, Federal, State, Final review, File. Medical expenses sit inside Federal rather than as their own item, so this screen is just the launch pad.

image.caption: The Tax Home dashboard after logging back into a return, with Federal in the left-hand checklist.

steps.heading: Open Federal, then Deductions & credits, then Medical
steps.body: Click Federal in the left sidebar, then choose Deductions & credits. A list of categories appears — home energy credits, dependent care credit, car registration fees, education expenses, HSA and MSA contributions, and Medical expenses near the bottom. TurboTax first asks a screening question along the lines of "Did you spend more than [a dollar amount] on medical expenses?" Answer honestly even if your total looks small; answering no here skips the section entirely, which is a common reason people can't find it again later.

image.caption: The Federal deductions list, with Medical expenses alongside HSA contributions and other credit categories.

steps.heading: Answer the category-by-category questions
steps.body: Once inside, TurboTax breaks costs into categories instead of one blank total field. One screen asks specifically about medical travel: lodging (the IRS caps this at $50 per person per night, with a Learn More link explaining the rule), other travel costs like bus, parking, or taxi fares, and miles driven to appointments. Fill in whatever applies and leave the rest blank; TurboTax skips categories that don't apply as you click Continue.

image.caption: The medical travel screen, asking separately for lodging, other travel costs, and miles driven to medical appointments.

steps.heading: Know what the IRS actually counts before you enter a number
steps.body: Per IRS Topic 502, deductible expenses cover diagnosis, treatment, cure, mitigation, or prevention of disease: doctor and dentist fees, prescription drugs and insulin, hospital and nursing home care, hearing aids, wheelchairs, and prescription eyeglasses, plus transportation that's primarily for and essential to medical care. Left out entirely: over-the-counter medicine, cosmetics, most cosmetic surgery, general wellness trips, and anything an employer or insurer already covered. TurboTax's Learn More links on each screen are worth opening the first time an unfamiliar category shows up.

steps.heading: Check the threshold before you expect a lower bill
steps.body: Only the amount above 7.5% of your adjusted gross income counts, and only if your itemized deductions beat the standard deduction for your filing status. On $50,000 of AGI, the floor is $3,750; $4,000 in expenses would deduct just $250. TurboTax runs this math automatically once you finish the section, so a total that doesn't move your refund isn't necessarily wrong. It matters more in a year with a major medical event.

steps.heading: Keep the backup for next year
steps.body: Save receipts, mileage logs, and statements in one place, physical or digital, as the year goes rather than reconstructing them next April. Self-employed filers in particular benefit from logging medical costs monthly alongside other deductible expenses, since self-employed health insurance premiums are claimed separately from this section as an above-the-line deduction, and mixing the two up costs time later.

troubleshooting.problem: Medical expenses were entered but the refund amount didn't change
troubleshooting.cause: The total, after subtracting 7.5% of AGI, either came to very little or your combined itemized deductions still didn't beat the standard deduction.
troubleshooting.fix: Compare your Schedule A total to your standard deduction for the year. If Schedule A doesn't win, TurboTax is correctly using the standard deduction instead.

troubleshooting.problem: The Medical expenses category doesn't show up under Deductions & credits anymore
troubleshooting.cause: The initial screening question ("Did you spend more than [amount] on medical expenses?") was answered no, which skips the section.
troubleshooting.fix: Use TurboTax's search box, type "medical expenses," and use the Jump to link to reopen the screening question and answer it again.

troubleshooting.problem: A large expense was entered but TurboTax's Learn More link says it doesn't qualify
troubleshooting.cause: Not all health-related spending counts. Cosmetic procedures, over-the-counter products, and anything already reimbursed are specifically excluded by the IRS.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the entry, or reduce it to only the unreimbursed, IRS-qualifying portion.

faq.question: Where exactly is the medical expenses section in TurboTax?
faq.answer: From Tax Home, open Federal in the left sidebar, then Deductions & credits, then Medical expenses. Answer the initial screening question honestly, since a "no" skips the section.

faq.question: What medical expenses actually qualify for a deduction?
faq.answer: IRS Topic 502 covers diagnosis, treatment, and prevention costs, plus related travel like mileage, lodging, and transportation to appointments. Over-the-counter medicine, cosmetics, and anything already reimbursed don't count.

faq.question: Is there a minimum before medical expenses reduce my taxes?
faq.answer: Yes. Only the amount above 7.5% of your adjusted gross income counts, and you need to itemize deductions rather than take the standard deduction to benefit at all.

faq.question: Do freelancers track medical expenses differently than employees?
faq.answer: The itemized deduction rules are the same, but self-employed health insurance premiums are claimed separately as an above-the-line deduction, not through this section.

faq.question: Why did my medical expenses section disappear after I said no to the first question?
faq.answer: TurboTax's screening question ("Did you spend more than [amount] on medical expenses?") controls whether the category shows up at all. Search for "medical expenses" and use Jump to in order to reopen it.
